- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative over 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward — apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.5) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate mean — apply mean reversion to forecast by subtracting 1–2% from average of last 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often lags — forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days post-peak.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weakly positive or neutral — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 periods if sentiment remains flat or slightly positive.
